findings: Official archived PTX12.1.1 and13.0.3 document applypriority.global.L2::evict_normal on global 128-byte aligned ranges, literal size128, PTX7.4 and SM80+. This supplies a direct scoped normalization contract absent from the original setter/free reasoning. It is not discard and is not a physical-residency measurement.

Whole owned prefix arithmetic is correct: 5,387,252 -> 5,387,136 bytes/42,087 lines with116-byte untouched tail;132 ->128 bytes/one line with4-byte tail. Require the actual base alignment and checked bounds; never round accesses beyond allocation. Exact stream/node extent readback must reject driver alignment mismatch. Runtime and compilation eligibility are both required.
CUDA12.1.1 explicitly allows prefetch of an absent line; normalizing can consume bandwidth and cannot be called free. No newer bulk instruction or global context/cache setter is needed or authorized.

Epoch cleanup is distinct from final teardown. Graphs may be retained while the allocation remains live and launches are quiesced. Mark dirty before fallible eager/captured submissions; disable/verify stream policy, issue bounded normalization, synchronize, then mark clean. Any failure stays failed/dirty. Rearm before a later deliberate epoch; final close forbids later launches and retires graph references before free.

The frozen evaluator calls full sync_to_cpu and synchronize before stopping readback and total timers. Completing disable/verification/normalization inside sync_to_cpu counts the new cost without evaluator changes. Destructor-only cleanup would not qualify; successful clean epochs should not be charged again silently on Drop.

Graph inheritance remains separately unproved. D064 stays capture-only, with no replay or normalization work added. A future separately authorized cleanup feasibility check can establish emitted instruction, address coverage, successful ordered completion and exact data, but cannot itself establish solver equivalence or performance.
